rules.title: 2026 Massachusetts Rent Control Ballot Question
rules.requirement: A proposed ballot question would have limited annual rent increases on residences statewide, but it was struck from the ballot by the Supreme Judicial Court because of a religious exemption that violated the state constitution's ban on religious ballot questions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to residential rental units statewide, with carve-outs for certain unit types including those used for religious purposes.
rules.exemptions: Units operated solely for religious purposes and other secular exemption categories.
rules.citation: Mass. 2026 Rent Control Ballot Question (struck by SJC)
rules.quoted_span: The proposal limits annual rent increases for residences, but it carved out exemptions for several types of units, including ones “operated solely for … religious … purposes."

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is operated solely for religious or other exempted purposes

rules.conflict_note: This ballot question was blocked by the Supreme Judicial Court and will not appear on the November 2026 ballot; it never became law.
